mainTopic: Why מעשר בהמה may not be sold (רב אשי's reading of 'לא יגאל'), and who may eat a blemished בכור
overview: The amud opens by looking for the source that a מעשר בהמה animal may not be sold. The first approach takes the extra words 'it shall not be redeemed' from חרמים and applies them to מעשר rather than to בכור, because מעשר also has the word 'redeem.' רב אשי offers a different source: 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' written by מעשר itself really means 'it shall not be sold.' He proves this because the words sit next to תמורה, which only works while the animal is alive, and an animal cannot be unredeemable alive but redeemable after שחיטה. The גמרא defends this proof against a challenge from the opinion that קדשי מזבח need no העמדה והערכה, and against the idea that weaker holiness makes redemption easier. It then explains why the תורה said 'redeemed' and not 'sold': the word teaches that both selling and redeeming are forbidden. A new משנה follows, where בית שמאי forbid a ישראל from eating a בכור with a כהן, and בית הלל allow it, even for a גוי. The גמרא shows that this משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and that בית שמאי learn their view from the comparison of the בכור to the חזה ושוק.

steps.title: Why does the תורה need the words 'it shall not be redeemed'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה wrote the words 'it shall not be redeemed' by חרמים, since they seem unnecessary there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words '[it shall not] be redeemed' that the תורה wrote, why do I need them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to words in the פסוק of חרמים that seem extra and asks why they are there. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will use those extra words for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When words in the תורה are not needed for their own topic, the גמרא often moves them to a related topic. Here the question 'why do I need it?' opens the door to using 'it shall not be redeemed' as a source for מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Why do I need it? Used when words look extra

phrases.english: 'Be redeemed,' which the Merciful One wrote
phrases.notes: The full quote is 'it shall not be redeemed,' said about חרמים.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose do the seemingly extra words 'it shall not be redeemed' serve?

steps.title: Apply the extra words to מעשר
steps.stepSummary: Since the words are not needed for חרמים, the גמרא uses them to teach a law about מעשר: it may not be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they are not needed for the topic of חרמים, apply them to the topic of מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra words teach about מעשר instead, giving us the source that מעשר may not be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule of אם אינו ענין: words with no job in their own place are moved to another topic. The result is that the ban on selling, which is clear by חרמים, also applies to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own topic
Items a person dedicates as חרם
Here, מעשר בהמה, the tenth animal set aside

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the topic of dedications,
apply it to the topic of the animal tithe.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words teach that מעשר may not be sold.

steps.title: Why not apply the words to בכור instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the extra words should go to בכור rather than מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: apply them to the topic of בכור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the extra words go to מעשר and not to בכור, which is also a holy animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once words are moved to another topic, we must explain why they went to this topic and not a different one. בכור seems just as good a choice, so the choice of מעשר needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, used to suggest another option
A firstborn animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: Say instead: apply it to the topic of a firstborn?

steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to apply the extra words to מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בכור is also a holy animal, so there is no clear reason to prefer מעשר.

steps.title: מעשר has the word 'redeem' just like חרמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מעשר is more similar to חרמים, because the word 'redeem' is written by both.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר has 'redemption' written by it, just like חרמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the extra words go to מעשר because the תורה uses the same word 'redeem' by מעשר as by חרמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared wording 'לא יגאל' ties מעשר to חרמים more closely than בכור. So the ban on selling that comes with that wording by חרמים carries over to מעשר.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the first approach, מעשר may not be sold because the extra 'לא יגאל' of חרמים is applied to it, since both use the word 'redeem.'

phrases.english: The tithe has redemption written by it, like it.
phrases.notes: 'Like it' means like חרמים. Both have 'it shall not be redeemed' in the פסוק.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shared wording links מעשר to חרמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words could just as well go to בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: They go to מעשר, which shares the word 'redeem' with חרמים.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'Not redeemed' by מעשר means 'not sold'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different source: the words 'it shall not be redeemed' written by מעשר itself really mean 'it shall not be sold.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'It shall not be redeemed' said about מעשר means it shall not be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new approach and does not need to borrow words from חרמים. He reads the words by מעשר itself as a ban on selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first approach, 'not redeemed' by מעשר meant real redemption, and the selling ban came from חרמים. רב אשי reads that same phrase by מעשר as meaning 'not sold.'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'It shall not be redeemed' said about the tithe —
means it shall not be sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא יגאל' by מעשר means it may not be sold.

steps.title: רב אשי brings his source פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes the פסוק where 'it shall not be redeemed' comes right after the rule of תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: How do I know this? Because it is written: 'And it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי quotes the פסוק his reading is built on. This sets up his proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that 'it shall not be redeemed' is placed together with תמורה, swapping a holy animal for another. רב אשי will use that link to show what 'redeemed' must mean.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an animal swapped for a holy one, which also becomes holy

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: From where do I say this?
As it is written: 'Then both it and its substitute
shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'

steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's reading that 'לא יגאל' means 'not sold'

steps.title: Real redemption after slaughter makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי shows that reading 'redeemed' literally leads to a problem: a slaughtered animal cannot go through העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does it make a תמורה? While alive. So when can it not be redeemed? While alive. That means after שחיטה it can be redeemed. But redemption needs העמדה והערכה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues that since תמורה only works while the animal is alive, the 'not redeemed' rule next to it also applies only while it is alive. That would mean it can be redeemed after שחיטה, which is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming a holy animal requires standing it before a כהן to be valued, and a dead animal cannot stand. So a literal reading of 'redeemed' does not work, and this pushes us toward 'sold.'

keyTerms.meaning: Standing the animal up and having it valued, needed for redemption

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying מעשר may really be redeemed after שחיטה. He shows that reading 'redeemed' literally would lead to that impossible result.

phrases.english: When does it make a substitute? While alive.
When may it not be redeemed? While alive.
This implies that after slaughter it may be redeemed.
But it requires standing and valuation!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:11–12. A slaughtered animal can't be stood up for the כהן to value.

steps.raayaObject: That 'לא יגאל' cannot mean literal redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: The link between תמורה and 'לא יגאל' in ויקרא 27:33, plus the need for העמדה והערכה

steps.title: So 'not redeemed' means 'not sold'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that 'it shall not be redeemed' by מעשר means it may not be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: 'it shall not be redeemed' means it shall not be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his proof: since literal redemption does not fit, the words must mean selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading it as 'not sold' fixes the problem. מעשר may not be sold while alive, like תמורה, but after שחיטה it may be sold, and selling a slaughtered animal needs no העמדה והערכה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, 'לא יגאל' by מעשר means 'not sold.' The ban applies only while the animal is alive; after שחיטה it may be sold.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit on the selling ban: it covers a live מעשר animal, not its meat after שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from this:
'It shall not be redeemed' means it shall not be sold.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'לא יגאל' by מעשר means it may not be sold while alive; after שחיטה it may be sold.

steps.title: The proof only works for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב אשי's proof from העמדה והערכה only works for the opinion that קדשי מזבח needed העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says altar-holy animals needed standing and valuation. But for the one who says they did not, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's proof from step 7. That proof assumed every holy animal must be stood up and valued before it is redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said a slaughtered animal cannot be redeemed because it cannot stand for העמדה והערכה. But one opinion holds that קדשי מזבח never needed העמדה והערכה at all. By that opinion, a slaughtered מעשר animal could be redeemed, and 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' could be read literally after all.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says (opens a challenge from another opinion)
Animals made holy to be brought on the altar
Standing the animal up and having it valued before redemption
What is there to say? (the other opinion is a problem)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
that animals holy for the altar were
included in standing and valuation,
phrases.notes: He means blemished altar animals: to redeem them, you first had to stand them up and have them valued.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says
that animals holy for the altar were not
included in standing and valuation,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof רב אשי used in step 7 to reach his conclusion in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's proof that a slaughtered animal cannot be redeemed because it cannot go through העמדה והערכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the opinion that קדשי מזבח do not need העמדה והערכה, the problem disappears, so 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' could still be read literally.

steps.title: The real point: no animal is redeemable only after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב אשי's point was not about העמדה והערכה. His point is that no animal is unredeemable while alive yet redeemable after slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we meant: is there any case where an animal cannot be redeemed while alive, but can be redeemed after it is slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reframes רב אשי's argument so that it works for every opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' meant no redemption, it would forbid redeeming the live animal while leaving the slaughtered one open. That strange split, unredeemable alive but redeemable after slaughter, does not exist anywhere. So the word must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we meant (clarifying an earlier argument)

phrases.english: This is what we meant:
is there anything that cannot be redeemed while alive,
and can be redeemed after slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by changing the basis of the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the argument: the proof rests on general logic, not on העמדה והערכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof depended on the need for העמדה והערכה, so it fails for the opinion that קדשי מזבח did not need it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof works for everyone: an animal cannot be redeemable only after slaughter.

steps.title: Maybe weaker holiness makes redemption possible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there could not be such a case. Once slaughtered, the animal's holiness is weaker, so maybe then it can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? While alive, its holiness is strong, so it cannot be redeemed. After slaughter, its holiness is lighter, so it can be redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim of step 10 by suggesting such a split actually makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that strong holiness locks the animal in, and weaker holiness lets it go. If so, 'unredeemable alive, redeemable after slaughter' is perfectly logical. Then 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' could be read literally again.

phrases.english: Why not?
While alive, when its holiness is strong,
it cannot be redeemed;
after slaughter, when its holiness has become lighter,
it can be redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of the answer given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that no animal can be redeemable only after slaughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holiness gets weaker after slaughter, so redemption should be easier then, which makes the split logical.

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion with a קל וחומר. Strong holiness transfers more easily, so if the live animal cannot be redeemed, the slaughtered one certainly cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it all the more so? If while alive, when it is strong enough to pass its holiness to its redemption money, it still cannot be redeemed, then after slaughter, when it is not strong enough, can it be redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 11 and shows the logic actually points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 assumed weaker holiness makes redemption easier. The גמרא says the reverse: strong holiness is better at moving onto something else, the way a live animal can make another animal holy through תמורה. So if even the live animal cannot be redeemed, the weaker slaughtered animal surely cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a קל וחומר)
To pass its holiness onto its redemption money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'weaker holiness' means 'easier to redeem.' Here the גמרא says strong holiness is the kind that transfers to money, so a weaker one is harder to redeem, not easier.

phrases.english: But isn't it all the more so?
If while alive,
when it is strong enough to pass its holiness to its redemption money,
it cannot be redeemed,
then after slaughter,
when it is not strong enough to pass its holiness to its redemption money,
can it be redeemed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 and restores the answer of step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion in step 11 that a slaughtered animal could be redeemed because its holiness is weaker.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes weaker holiness transfers more easily, when really strong holiness is the kind that transfers to money.

steps.title: So 'it shall not be redeemed' means 'it shall not be sold'
steps.stepSummary: Since a literal reading does not work, the גמרא concludes that 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' means 'it may not be sold.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: 'It shall not be redeemed' means 'it shall not be sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: After defending the argument, the גמרא restates רב אשי's conclusion, now standing on firmer ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 9 is answered, and the side attack in step 11 is pushed off. The only sensible reading left is that the פסוק forbids selling the מעשר animal. This works for every opinion about העמדה והערכה.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
'It shall not be redeemed' means 'it shall not be sold.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:33, the פסוק about מעשר בהמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the objection-defense cycle by reaffirming the conclusion of step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' by מעשר means the animal may not be sold, and this holds for every opinion.

steps.title: Why not just write 'it shall not be sold'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the meaning is 'not sold,' why didn't the תורה just say 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the תורה write 'it shall not be sold'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the פסוק. If it means selling, why use the word 'redeemed'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The conclusion of step 13 makes the תורה's word choice look odd. If the point is 'do not sell,' the clear word would be 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר.' The גמרא wants a reason for the indirect wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let the תורה write (asks why it did not use clearer wording)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: Then let the Torah write 'it shall not be sold'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 13 based on the wording of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' as 'it shall not be sold.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meaning is selling, the תורה should have used the plain word for selling.

steps.title: 'Redeemed' teaches both selling and redeeming are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Had the תורה written 'not sold,' we would think only selling is forbidden but redeeming is allowed. Writing 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' teaches that both are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written 'it shall not be sold,' I would have said only selling is forbidden, since that treats it like an ordinary item, but redeeming is allowed, since the money goes to הקדש. So the תורה wrote 'it shall not be redeemed': it may not be sold and it may not be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 14 by showing why the word 'redeemed' was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling seems worse, because the holy animal is traded like everyday property. Redeeming seems fine, because its value goes into הקדש. By choosing 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל,' the תורה blocks redeeming too, while the word still also covers selling.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple treasury, property set aside as holy

steps.whatToRemember: By מעשר בהמה, 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' forbids two things: it may not be sold, and it may not be redeemed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one word in the פסוק carries both bans. The word 'redeem' was chosen because it names the gentler-looking act, so it teaches that even redeeming is forbidden, not only selling.

phrases.english: If the Torah had written 'it shall not be sold,'
I would have said:
it is only selling that is not allowed,
because one is treating it like an ordinary item,
but redeeming is allowed,
since its money goes into הקדש.
Therefore the Torah wrote 'it shall not be redeemed,'
teaching that it may not be sold
and it may not be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the wording: a different word would have led to a wrong conclusion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר,' only selling would be forbidden, and redemption would be allowed because the money goes to הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל' forbids both selling and redeeming the מעשר animal.

steps.title: The משנה: may a non-priest join a priest in eating a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי forbid a ישראל from being counted with a כהן to eat a בכור. בית הלל permit it, and even a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: a ישראל may not be counted with the כהן for the בכור. בית הלל permit it, and even a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It records an argument about who may join a group eating the meat of a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold the meat is for כהנים only, so a ישראל cannot be part of the group. בית הלל allow non-כהנים, and the משנה adds that even a גוי may join. That last phrase, 'even a גוי,' is what the גמרא will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: be counted: signed up as part of a group that eats together
a firstborn male animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִמָּנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַכֹּהֵן לַבְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: An Israelite may not be counted with the priest for eating the firstborn,
and Beit Hillel permit it,
and even a gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: לֹא יִמָּנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַכֹּהֵן לַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of 'לא יגאל' ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: only כהנים may eat a בכור together. בית הלל: non-כהנים may join, even a גוי.

steps.title: Whose view is this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which Sage the משנה follows. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'even a גוי' are a strong claim to put in the name of בית הלל. The גמרא wants to know who reports בית הלל's view this broadly.

keyTerms.meaning: whose is it? which Sage taught it?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Whose view is our Mishnah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who wrote the view in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's version of בית הלל appears in the משנה, especially the words 'even a גוי'.

steps.title: It is רבי עקיבא, as shown by a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא. A ברייתא shows that he reports בית הלל as allowing even a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי עקיבא, as a ברייתא teaches: for a בכור, only a group made up entirely of כהנים may be counted. That is the view of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: even non-כהנים. רבי עקיבא permits even a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. It proves this from a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא allows even a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, בית הלל are quoted as allowing only 'זרים,' meaning non-כהנים. רבי עקיבא is the one who extends their view to a גוי. Since our משנה says 'even a גוי,' it must follow רבי עקיבא's version.

keyTerms.meaning: are counted, signed up to eat

steps.confusionAlert: 'זרים' here does not mean strangers or non-Jews. It means Jews who are not כהנים. The גוי is a separate, further step.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Akiva,
as it is taught in a baraita:
A firstborn: people may not be counted to eat it
except a group made up entirely of priests;
this is the statement of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say: even non-priests.
Rabbi Akiva permits even a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of whose view the משנה is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who reports that בית הלל permit even a גוי. The proof is a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where בית הלל allow זרים and רבי עקיבא extends this to a גוי.

steps.title: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind בית שמאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why בית שמאי limit the בכור to כהנים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's view is the stricter one, so the גמרא looks for the פסוק behind it.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After naming the views, the גמרא asks for the reasoning of the strict view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for limiting the בכור to כהנים.

steps.title: The firstborn is compared to the breast and thigh
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'their flesh shall be yours' compares the בכור to the חזה ושוק. Just as only כהנים eat those, only כהנים eat the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And their flesh shall be yours, etc.' Just as there, כהנים may eat and ישראלים may not, so too here, כהנים may eat and ישראלים may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's source: a פסוק that compares the בכור's meat to the חזה ושוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the פסוק says the meat is yours 'like the breast of waving and the right thigh.' Those parts are only for כהנים and their families. By comparison, the בכור's meat is also only for כהנים, so a ישראל cannot join the group.

keyTerms.meaning: and their flesh shall be yours (said to the כהן)
just as there... so too here: a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי learn from the comparison to חזה ושוק that only כהנים may eat a בכור. בית הלל allow non-כהנים, and according to רבי עקיבא even a גוי, which is the view in our משנה.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And their flesh shall be yours, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:18. The פסוק continues 'like the breast of waving and the right thigh.'

phrases.english: Just as there, priests: yes,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the breast and thigh named in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: Israelites: no,
so too here, priests: yes,
Israelites: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about בית שמאי's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares the בכור to the חזה ושוק, which only כהנים eat, so only כהנים may eat the בכור.
